title: Duke Rudolf August of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel → his son-in-law Duke Johann Adolf of Plön: 500-800 letters with ciphered political passages, key printed, only about ten extracts read
correspondents: Rudolf August of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel → Johann Adolf of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Plön
shelfmark: Landesarchiv Schleswig-Holstein, Abt. 20 (Herzöge von Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Plön), Nr. 40 a-d
folio_note: four bundles, letters 1676-1703 (first ciphered letter 26 Feb / 7 Mar 1676); runs of signs from a few words to whole sentences inside clear text; heaviest from 1690
status: Birkner, "Eine Plön-Wolfenbütteler Geheimschrift", Zeitschrift der Gesellschaft für Schleswig-Holsteinische Geschichte 136 (2011) pp. 89-98, describes the cipher (monoalphabetic signs, partly Greek letters, dots and strokes for a, e, i, o; no word breaks), prints the sign table (fig. 2) and reads about ten extracts (1681-1698). He says the rest of the correspondence is unexploited. Not in cyphersolver catalogue (checked: Abt. 20 appears only as key Nr. 37 in entry 604); entry 2020 (NLA Wolfenbüttel 2 Alt Nr. 3565, Rudolf August to Heimburg) may share the system.
why: A ducal channel kept secret from co-regent Anton Ulrich: Brunswick politics, the electoral dignity, Celle, Vienna and the Dutch war, 1676-1703; the key is in print, so the unread passages are readable.
score_note: Scored from Birkner 2011 (open access, SUB Hamburg) during the Nov 2026 editions pass (L'Europe chiffrée, 25 Nov 2026); originals not viewed

title: Antonio de Guaras (London) → Don John of Austria, intercepted Spanish cipher letters, partly read with gaps
correspondents: Antonio de Guaras → Don John of Austria
shelfmark: TNA SP 70/143 (Foreign Various, Elizabeth I, Feb 1577), Crosby CSP Foreign 1575-77 no. 1264; 'two letters of Antony Guerras' sent by Wilson to Walsingham 10 Mar 1577 (CSP no. 1326) probably SP 70/144
folio_note: CSP no. 1264: 'Letter in Spanish cipher intercepted', Pp. 1½ (~1½ pages of cipher, plain Spanish added in the margin per Wilson); the calendar gives no folio
status: Calendar gives no reading. But Kervyn de Lettenhove, Relations politiques t. IX no. MMMCCCLIX pp. 200-201 prints a Spanish text (source 'Record office, Cal. n° 1264') with lacunae (rows of dots) and bracketed words, and t. X no. MMMDCXL pp. 69-70 a contemporary French translation (Record Office 'Pap. of Flanders vol. 31 p. 118', filed among Nov 1577 papers) with the same lacunae: so a contemporary decipherment exists but is PARTIAL (names/words left blank). Marnix (St Aldegonde) wrote 12 Mar 1577 that he could not read the ciphers from copies, then (Wilson 22 Mar, CSP 1360) 'has deciphered Guerras letters first into Spanish then French'. Not on Daniel's catalogue (cat. 303=1001 is the 1574 letter). Not checked against DECODE.
why: Key of Guaras's personal nomenclator with Don John (numbers such as 82, 29, 38 named in his 1578 interrogation); the lacunae are names (Elizabeth's circle, Leicester, Mary Stuart) and a key would read his other cipher letters 1577-78.
score_note: Scored from the printed calendar/Kervyn text during the 25 Nov 2026 CSP Foreign sweep (research/csp-foreign-guaras-1577-2026-11-25/); original not viewed
verify: Order/view SP 70/143 (Gale State Papers Online or TNA Kew; not digitised on TNA Discovery) and find the ciphertext of no. 1264 and the second letter; compare with Kervyn t. IX pp. 200-201 and t. X pp. 69-70 to align ciphertext and plaintext.
